text: The Patriots' turnover troubles proved costly in their 30-24 Thursday night loss to the Bears, a defeat that underscores Mike Vrabel's emphasis on turnover differential as a cornerstone of team identity—and one area where New England is clearly struggling after falling to Caleb Williams and Chicago. The loss came without starting guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown, making an already difficult offensive line situation worse, though Rhamondre Stevenson did provide one bright spot by reaching a career high in receiving yards and continuing his reliable work in the backfield. Drake Maye's film from the loss reveals the growing pains of a young quarterback facing a stiff defensive challenge, and the Patriots defense, despite some strong moments, couldn't quite stymie the Bears' attack when it mattered most. With Vrabel's four-pillar philosophy demanding better execution on both sides of the ball, the film and stats from Chicago make clear that New England has significant work to do if it wants to climb back into contention.
